title: fix: automations switch accounts when interactive defaults change

test(cron): read private bindings through persisted store

The latest scheduled main run now reproduces the four cron seed failures from the Page polish run: `38663143259` at `a10ae12e01bdcb5f4214bad403edf1512bf96561`, real-Gateway shard 2 (`116189130280`). All four exact test names and their first AssertionError signatures match Page run `38659104160` after removing timestamps: the CLI returns exit code 1 before UI interaction. Earlier scheduled main `38654297528` passed them. The latest evidence establishes these as current main failures; it does not yet identify the underlying rejection.

The source lead remains the creation-time prerequisite introduced here: `cron.add` calls `captureCronCreatorSession`; isolated `agentTurn` jobs without a runtime grant enter `captureCronInferenceForCaller`, which resolves model/session auth and prepares route-aware runtime auth. The primary fixture in `cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` supplies Gateway and disabled-cron/failure-alert configuration, without a model/account fixture. This is a lead, not a confirmed diagnosis; production authority checks must remain intact.

The fixture already records redacted CLI stderr, but emits its command records only during capture mode. Page PR #171858 now carries a reviewed diagnostic-only assertion message that includes that existing redacted stderr. Its next CI run will expose the exception without weakening the exit-code assertion. The native inherited-failure guard correctly refuses that changed test source, so we will inspect the exception and repair the fixture if warranted, or retire the diagnostic after it has served its purpose. No guard bypass is proposed.

[Original four-case evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171987#issuecomment-6181624059).

## Existing cron jobs fail after a routine update

A source-checkout install was updated to `22e0839`, which includes this PR. After the update, its existing isolated `agentTurn` jobs began to fail on their first scheduled run:

```text
Automation has no recorded inference account. Explicitly select its account with a model@profile update before running it.
```

**What we saw:**
- The install has 14 isolated `agentTurn` jobs. Eleven of them name one OpenAI model, which runs through stored OAuth credentials.
- The install has exactly **one** OpenAI auth profile: `openai:default`.
- Two jobs that ran after the update both failed with the error above:
  - an hourly sync job failed on its first run, about one minute after the update;
  - a daily job failed at its 08:00 run.
- Jobs that last ran before the update still show `ok`. Each will probably fail at its next run. We cannot see whether a job has a binding, so we cannot list them exactly.
- `failureAlert` worked: the owner received "failed 2 times … an automatic repair was requested in its owner conversation; it is still failing". The automatic repair could not fix it, because adoption requires an explicit `model@profile` edit.
- Doctor and the updater gave no warning about these jobs before the update or after it.

**Why this matters:** the user changed no setting. A routine update turned working automations into failing ones. On this install the account was never in doubt: every job ran on `openai:default` before the update, and that is still the only OpenAI profile.

## Proposal: record the account once at upgrade, without refusing

The protection this PR adds is still right: after a job has an account, later changes to defaults or profile order must not move it. The one change we propose is for jobs that have no binding yet:

1. **One-time migration** in Doctor and startup, before any old job runs again. Each job without a binding records the profile that the old resolution picks at migration time, which is the account it used on every earlier run.
   - This keeps today's behavior. It is not guessing from future defaults, and after the migration this PR's protection applies in full.
   - Back up the cron state before writing, and log each recorded account.
2. **Refuse only when the account is unclear.** For example: the old resolution finds no stored profile, or it picks one that no longer exists. In that case, Doctor should warn before the update and print the exact `cron edit --model <model>@<profile>` command. The run error should name the profile the job used to pick.
3. Optional: record the profile each run used in the run history. Then later migrations can use real evidence instead of reconstructing it.

Related work (#172717, #172735, #172709, #172683) covers CLI-backed jobs and test fixtures. None of it covers jobs created before this PR. #172717 keeps "explicit adoption" for these jobs, so this needs agreement from the owners before anyone writes it. @fuller-stack-dev @steipete, would you accept a migration along these lines? If so, we can prepare the PR.

## Proposed rule for jobs created before account binding (follow-up to #172792 and #173411)

**Rule:** a job with no recorded account gets the account its next unbound run would use: an explicit selection, or else the first account from the runtime's normal account planner. Refuse only when no account fits, or when that account is another person's personal login. A key in env or provider config, or an AWS SDK route that the provider config declares, has no stored account to record. Such a job stays unbound and runs on that credential, and job creation follows the same rule.

**Why this keeps your guarantee:** before #172590, every unbound run took that planner's first account. Recording it once changes nothing that day. After that, the binding is fixed, so later changes to defaults or profile order cannot move the job; that is the protection #172590 added. This is not run telemetry or `lastUsed` used as authority. Doctor calls the same `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` (with the same provider preferred-profile hook) that a run calls. The Doctor log names every other eligible account and the `automations edit … --model …@<profileId>` command.

**What changes today:** with several eligible accounts, Doctor only warns, and the job then fails every run until someone edits it. That breaks the "updates always work" rule. Creating a job on a provider-config key is also refused, which is inconsistent with #173411, where old jobs on the same key keep running.

**Census of four real installs** (Doctor preview, read-only):

| Install | Unbound agent-turn jobs | Configured key | One eligible account | Several eligible | Personal | Missing | Native/runtime |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A (source, 2026.10.3) | 15 | 15 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| B (container, 2026.10.3) | 19 | 0 | 19 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| C (container, 2026.10.3) | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 3 |
| D (2026.10.1) | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 |

Install B runs a build from before #172792, and 4 of its jobs fail at this moment with "no recorded inference account". The next update fixes them through #172792's single-account path. None of the four installs is in the "several eligible accounts" case, but any install with both an API key and a subscription login for one provider is.

Implementation: #173509. @fuller-stack-dev @steipete, does this rule work for you? I will not merge it without a reply from one of you.
